proposition: Under the map n -> n/2 when n is even, n -> 3n+1 when n is odd, every integer n with 1 <= n <= 529564 reaches 1 in fewer than 383 steps.
hypotheses: the stopping time counts steps until the value 1 is reached

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 50, the stopping time of n is less than 383.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2335, the stopping time of n is less than 383.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000 for which n^2 > 1000.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 805 modulo 161.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n*(n+1) is at least 2*n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
The steps above establish the statement up to 2335, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 529564.
